votes.reason: The 14.1x trailing multiple rests on EPS up 389.7% from record crack spreads driven by a supply shock, which is the top of the cycle where a refiner's low P/E is least reliable, and after a +38.9% 12-week run the price leaves no margin of safety if margins return to normal.
At 11.1x trailing it is the cheapest name in the book, EPS is still growing 10.1%, and it is a disciplined top-tier insurer, so it is both cheap and sound.

At 38.2x trailing the stock is fully priced, but 34.9% EPS growth roughly supports that multiple for a profitable business, and its -19.6% 12-week fall has already taken some of the premium out, so my lens finds no concrete reason against it.
At 38.6x trailing against 83.1% EPS growth, NVDA is cheap for its growth and a dominant, highly profitable business, and its Aug 26 report comes after this week's close.
At 16.0x trailing with 43.9% EPS growth, GS is reasonably priced for a sound, top-tier franchise, and at 2.98% weekly volatility it is the steadiest name in the book.
